segments.text: In the Encyclopedia of Triangle Centers, erecting equilateral triangles outward and inward on the three sides of triangle A B C generates two celebrated pairs of central triangles: the outer and inner Isogonic Triangles, and the outer and inner Napoleon Triangles.

segments.text: Connecting the three outer equilateral apexes to the opposite vertices A, B, C yields three equal segments concurring at the First Fermat Point X thirteen at sixty-degree angles; the inner apexes concur at the Second Fermat Point X fourteen. Meanwhile, by Napoleon's Theorem, the centroids of the three outer equilateral triangles form a strictly equilateral triangle—the Outer Napoleon Triangle—and the inner centroids form the Inner Napoleon Triangle.

segments.text: Both Napoleon triangles share the exact same centroid X two as reference triangle A B C, their area difference equals the area of A B C, and their perspectors with A B C are the First and Second Napoleon Points X seventeen and X eighteen.
